label: Lookup (all rows)
gloss: read every matching row from a store as a list, not just the first one
why: A one-row lookup answers "which PO does this invoice bill against". A daily run needs the other question: "everything in the batch". Lookup in mode all returns a list of rows and attaches it to the record under one name. At Beacon, the 2:30 PM run reads the whole Payment Batch as batch, then counts it, totals it, and lists it in the run document.
cue: if the next step needs a count, a total, or a line per row, you need all the rows, not the first match
task: Collect the day: read every row of the Payment Batch and attach the list to the run as batch.
notes: Mode: all. With no match fields, every row in the store is returned.
The result is a list (3 rows here), not a single row - batch.invoiceNumber means nothing; batch is the whole list.
Mode one with no match fields is an error; mode all is how you read a whole table.

checks.label: The run carries batch (the list of Payment Batch rows)
